I've been wanting to learn c++ for awhile now. I know it will make me a better programmer and have a better understanding of what I'm doing. Most of my experience in programming is CLI commands and python/php. However, I've always had a hard time focus and retaining info while reading. I figured...Maybe, it wouldn't be a bad idea to try the whole learn while doing method.

The plan here is:

  1. Create a text-based environment where you can go N/S/E/W and look around.
  2. Add more actions (than just look / move)
  3. Add battling.
  4. Add items/inventory/equips.
  5. Expand the world
  6. Create a multiplayer function (Chatting with others while playing)

Would anyone say this is an alright way to go about learning c++? Basically, if I come across a program, instead of looking up a guide on things like "How to create IM/Client" I look up what knowledge I have, and try to build from my own known logic. (This way, it forces my problem solving to grow, instead of relying on S/O or anything like that.)

Any replies are appreciated.

I think this is definitely a good way to get into a language, though you might fall into bad habits since you'll most likely be just grabbing the things that you need without really learning the formalities of the language. I'd recommend getting a formal book on C++ to slowly work through as you work on your MUD, so you can pick up on the way professionals interact with the language.

Good luck!!!
Thank you for the recommendation. I've got my hands on a c++ book, so hopefully that will make things go smoother and help me have a more well-rounded understanding. :)

Any recommendations on a good book? I'm in a similar spot where I'm a coder trying to move into C++. I just went through the stuff on cplusplus.com's tutorials and then a lot of stackoverflow answers/blog's.

You may be in for a lot more than you bargained for. Unlike most, I will not try to dissuade you. I've started this path myself and I managed to survive it but it is extremely hard.

Multiplayer requires knowledge of Unix Sockets. The defacto starting point for absolutely everyone on sockets seems to be Beej's Guide. If you truly want to build from scratch this is the way to do it.

If you have absolutely no interest in sockets, you can start from a slightly more implemented and barebones MUD that Nick Gammon wrote called TinyMud. Here is his Forum Posting where he walks you through version 2. I recommend reading through it as you will learn how he decided to structure it. The GitHub code is available here if you want to fork it and work from there.

From my experience, start with Nick Gammon's server. Fork the project and work from there. When you are comfortable with how and why he implemented the socket programming the way he did, feel free to start your own and build it all from the ground up. I'll be honest, to read through a lot of his code is impossible unless you have some basic understanding of how to use FILE and Sockets.

I've forked his project myself and gotten quite a ways. An interesting approach is to start from his and implement MCCP (MUD Client Compression Protocol). This would be considered as step two in socket programming. Afterwards, adding in colour support is a good way to go.

I'm very passionate about the MUD community and always want to encourage people to get into coding for it. Let me know if you ever need any help.
